items.title: Could this ancient Greek idea make us be…
items.source: TED Talks · Daily · 个人学习用
sentences: More than 2,000 years ago in ancient Athens, young citizens were required to complete “ephebeia,” a two-year civic service program that taught them the laws of the city and how to defend their democracy.
Author and historian Scott Reich believes this practice reflects something crucial we often forget: citizens aren’t born — they’re trained.
In a hopeful talk, he shares his plan to bring a modern version of this program to the United States and explains why it could benefit everyone.

items.source: TED Talks · Daily · 个人学习用
sentences: Have you heard the clean energy transition is failing?
Energy analyst Michael Liebreich says to look again.
Using a four-line spreadsheet model of the global energy system, he shows why fossil fuels will inevitably get squeezed out over time — with no bans required.
The shift is well underway, he explains: it just looks different than many of us expected.

items.title: Your phone is disgusting. Here's how to …
items.source: TED Talks · Daily · 个人学习用
sentences: What’s dirtier: your phone or your hands?
Molecular biologist Lotti Tajouri says there’s a gaping hole in our hygiene routine.
We scrub our hands clean, then reach right for the phone — a warm, humid and mobile home for bacteria and viruses.
He explores the unnervingly vibrant microbial world living on your phone and shows how you can keep this “third hand” clean.

sentences: When life gets uncertain, do you grip a little tighter?

Drawing on brain research and her own struggles with uncertainty, she shares practical ways to let go and make room for creativity, calm and flow.
